narrative:
The model estimated a 41% probability that you would be a bad credit risk. That was above the bank’s risk cutoff, so your application was denied. This does not mean default is certain; it means your current financial profile looks riskier than the bank is willing to accept.

The strongest factor was your checking account balance being below zero. Among approved applicants, only about one in eight had a negative checking balance, while most had no negative balance. Because this was the most influential issue, it pushed your prediction strongly toward bad credit.

The next two most important factors actually worked in your favor. Your installment rate—2.00, below the approved average of 2.99—suggests a lighter monthly repayment burden, so it pushed toward good credit. Your requested loan duration of 12 months, shorter than the approved average of about 19 months, also helped by limiting how long you would be in debt. However, these positive signals were not enough to offset the negative checking account signal.

To improve your chances, focus on bringing your checking account into good standing and avoiding overdrafts. Keep your installment burden low, maintain stable employment, and consider reapplying once your checking account shows a healthier pattern. A guarantor or stronger savings could also help, but resolving the negative balance is the most important step.
